```
6  Email list size     - a total that only grows, so it never signals a problem
2  Blog visitors       - useful, but sign-ups measure the same traffic better
9  Reviews received    - matters for advocacy, not for this objective
```

**Check yourself.** The ruled-out list matters as much as the chosen one. If you
kept followers or total page views, re-read the vanity metric test in lesson 8:
if this number doubled, would the business be better off, and can you say how?

---

## Work in this

:::template Lab worksheet
EXERCISE 1 - PERSONA
Name and age:
Evidence (which review numbers):
Situation:
Goal:
Barriers:
Where they look:
So what - website:
So what - message:
So what - channel:
Second buyer spotted:

EXERCISE 2 - FUNNEL MAP
Awareness:
Interest:
Consideration:
Conversion:
Retention:
Advocacy:
The stage with no asset:
What I would build for it, and why:

EXERCISE 3 - KPIs
Objective:
1.                      Leading / lagging     Why:
2.                      Leading / lagging     Why:
3.                      Leading / lagging     Why:
4.                      Leading / lagging     Why:
5.                      Leading / lagging     Why:
Which KPI would reveal the gap, and how it would look:
What I ruled out, and why:
:::

## Self-check

Go through this before you move on. Each line is something the expected output
does.

:::checklist Lab self-check
- My persona is built only from the reviews, not from things I imagined
- Every barrier in my persona points at a specific review
- My persona has a "so what" line that changes a real decision
- I spotted that there are two different buyers in the reviews
- Every one of the six assets is placed at a stage
- I named consideration as the empty stage, or defended a different answer
- What I would build addresses the gap rather than adding more traffic
- I chose five KPIs or fewer
- At least two of my KPIs are leading indicators
- I can explain, for each KPI, how the business would be better off if it moved
- I wrote down what I ruled out and why
- I can say which KPI pair would reveal the consideration gap
:::

## What good looks like

A good submission is short and traceable. Every claim in the persona points at a
review number. The funnel gap is named and the fix addresses that gap rather
than defaulting to "get more traffic". The KPI list is five or fewer, includes
leading indicators, and comes with a list of what was deliberately left out.

If you cannot explain why something is on your KPI list, it should not be.

lessons.title: Assignment: a one-page digital marketing brief
lessons.description: Produce a one-page brief for a fictional brand, marked out of 100 against a published rubric.
lessons.content:
## The brief

Produce a **one-page digital marketing brief** for one of the four fictional
brands used in this course, or for a real small business you know well.

Pick one:

- **Petal & Pine** — a D2C skincare brand selling online, no shops
- **Bright Mile Dental** — a single-location dental clinic
- **Shiftly** — B2B shift-scheduling software sold to operations managers
- **Craftwise Academy** — an online course seller
- A real business you know well enough to describe honestly

If you choose a real business, use only what you can observe. Do not invent
figures for it, and do not present guesses as facts.

## What to submit

One page. Not two. The constraint is part of the assignment: a strategy nobody
can hold in their head does not get followed.

It must contain all seven sections below, in this order:

1. **Business objective** — what the business needs, with a number and a date
2. **Audience and persona** — one persona with situation, goal, barriers and
   where they look
3. **Segments** — two or three segments, each with the rule that defines it
4. **Journey stage** — the stage where the business is losing people, and how
   you know
5. **Channels** — two channels you would use with a reason each, and one you
   would deliberately not use with a reason
6. **Message and offer** — what you want people to understand, and what you are
   asking them to do
7. **KPIs** — a maximum of five, each labelled leading or lagging, each with a
   target

:::template Submission cover sheet
Name:
Brand chosen:
Real or fictional:
Time spent:
The hardest section to write, and why:
One thing I would research first if this were a real job:
:::

## Marking rubric

Marked out of 100. A pass is 50.

| Criterion | Marks | What earns full marks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Business objective | 15 | Specific, has a number and a date, and is plausible for a business of this size |
| Audience and persona | 20 | All four parts present; barriers are specific rather than generic; includes a "so what" that changes a decision |
| Segments | 15 | Two or three segments, each with a rule a tool could actually select on, and a different message for each |
| Journey stage | 10 | Names one stage, explains how you would know it is the weak one, and does not default to "we need more traffic" |
| Channels | 15 | Two channels with reasons tied to where the audience already looks, plus one channel deliberately ruled out with a reason |
| Message and offer | 10 | One clear idea, a specific ask, and a reason the audience would say yes |
| KPIs | 15 | Five or fewer, correctly labelled leading or lagging, at least two leading, each with a target and a stated reason for mattering |

**Marks are deducted for:**

- Going over one page — up to 10 marks
- Inventing data or performance figures about a real company — the Audience and
  Segments criteria score zero
- Promising a specific ranking, income or result — up to 10 marks
- A persona with no "so what" line — it scores at most half on that criterion

### Grade bands

| Marks | Band | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 85–100 | Distinction | Could be handed to a client with minor edits |
| 70–84 | Strong pass | Sound reasoning throughout; one or two sections thin |
| 50–69 | Pass | The chain holds together but several sections are generic |
| Below 50 | Resubmit | The brief is a list of tactics rather than a chain of decisions |

## What good looks like

The test for this assignment is the chain from lesson 9. A marker should be able
to start at your KPIs and work upwards: this KPI exists because of this message,
which exists because of this journey stage, which matters because of this
persona, who was chosen because of this objective.

If any link is missing, the brief is a list of tactics with a cover page.

The second test is the channel you ruled out. A brief that approves everything
has made no decisions, and deciding what not to do is the most valuable thing
on the page.

lessons.title: Assessment: digital marketing fundamentals
lessons.description: A ten-question closing quiz on the whole module, with a pass mark of 7 out of 10.
lessons.content:
## Before you start

Ten questions drawn from the whole module, not from any single lesson. This is
separate from the practice questions earlier — those were for learning, this is
for checking.

**Pass mark: 7 out of 10.**

If you score below 7, go back to the lessons named at the end of the practice
questions page rather than retaking this immediately. Nothing is recorded, and
retaking a quiz you have just seen the answers to teaches you nothing.

## The assessment

:::quiz
Q. A business spends everything on getting found and nothing on getting chosen. What is the most likely result?
+ Plenty of visitors and very few customers
- Few visitors and many customers
- Steady growth in repeat purchases
- Lower advertising costs
= Traffic without persuasion produces visitors who leave. All three jobs depend on each other.

Q. Which pairing is correct?
+ Earned media — a search ranking you did not pay for
- Owned media — a sponsored post
- Paid media — your email list
- Earned media — a banner advertisement
= Owned is what you control, earned is given to you by others, paid is rented.

Q. A business reaches its whole audience through a single social media account. What is the main risk?
+ A platform change could remove its access to that audience overnight
- The content will become repetitive
- It will spend too much on advertising
- Search engines will rank it lower
= It is building on rented land. Owned media is the only audience that cannot be taken away.

Q. At which funnel stage is a discount code most likely to be wasted?
+ Awareness
- Conversion
- Retention
- Consideration
= Someone who has just heard of you is not deciding on price yet. The discount gives away margin to people who were never close to buying.

Q. A B2B deal stalls after the user is convinced. What is the most likely cause?
+ Nobody gave the user something they could forward to the budget holder
- The product demonstration was too long
- The price was displayed too early
- The user did not understand the product
= B2B decisions involve several people. Enthusiasm from someone who cannot sign does not move anything on its own.

Q. Which of these is an actual segment?
+ Customers who bought more than six months ago and have not returned
- Customers who value quality
- Customers who would probably like our new product
- Customers in our target market
= A segment must be selectable in a tool. Purchase date is; an attitude you have never recorded is not.

Q. Why are leading indicators worth tracking?
+ They move early enough that you can still change the outcome
- They are easier to collect than lagging indicators
- They always look better in a report
- They replace the need for lagging indicators
= Lagging indicators tell you what happened after it is too late to act. Leading indicators let you steer.

Q. A marketing report shows impressions up 300% and enquiries flat. What is the honest reading?
+ Reach grew without producing results, so something after the impression is failing
- The campaign is working well
- The impressions figure must be wrong
- Enquiries will follow automatically
= Impressions rise whenever you spend more. Flat enquiries means the problem is further down the funnel.

Q. Which is the strongest source for building a buyer persona?
+ Reviews, support questions and conversations with actual customers
- A team brainstorm
- A competitor's marketing page
- The most confident opinion in the room
= Evidence beats imagination. A persona built in a meeting usually describes the team.

Q. What single test separates a strategy from a list of tactics?
+ Every tactic can be traced back up to the business objective
- It is written down and approved
- It covers every available channel
- It includes a budget
= The chain is the strategy. A tactic that cannot be traced back up it should not be funded.
:::

## Before you move on

The one thing module 2 assumes you already know: **a channel sends people
somewhere, and that destination decides whether the effort was worth anything.**

Module 2 is about that destination — websites, landing pages, calls to action
and forms — and it is where you write your first code.
